title: Vacuuming rooms with a backpack or upright machine
audience: Cleaners who vacuum carpet, hard floors and furniture in offices, shared buildings and homes using backpack or upright machines.
learningOutcomes: Set up a backpack or upright vacuum safely, including harness fit and cord handling.
Vacuum a room in a fixed direction so that corners, edges and under-desk areas are reached.
Apply the site's door-status marking and outlet-selection rules correctly, and leave each room as the client expects.

instruction.heading: Check the machine before you plug it in
instruction.body: Start in the cleaning cupboard with the machine. Inspect the collection bag or bin, the filter set and the cord. Look along the cord for cuts, scrapes, or bare conductors, and check the plug for damage. If a plug has lost its earth pin, do not use the machine; tag it and report it. A backpack machine should be fitted to the body before you start. Adjust the harness so the weight sits on the hips rather than the shoulders, and clip the tools onto the waist belt so they do not drag.

instruction.heading: Route and direction
instruction.body: Work in a consistent direction through each room so that you do not walk back over finished areas. A counter-clockwise route from the door works well for most rooms. Enter the room, turn right as you go in, and work around the perimeter back to the door. Vacuum the corners, edges and the areas under desks as you pass them, and push chairs in to the desk so that the floor beneath them is reached. Then clear the centre of the room with overlapping passes.

instruction.heading: Power, cords and outlets
instruction.body: Use the outlets that the site has identified for vacuuming. Many sites mark these with a coloured dot so that they are not confused with outlets that power equipment. Never disconnect a computer or similar equipment to free an outlet. Let the cord hang loosely so the plug is never under strain, and disconnect by gripping the plug body, not the cord. Plan the cord route so that you do not cross a path where people walk.

instruction.heading: Bins, furniture and mats
instruction.body: Look for a bin that has not been emptied. If one is found, lift it, vacuum underneath, and return it to the exact spot it came from. For furniture that is upholstered, use the upholstery tool with the hose, and spot clean only where the soil is visible. Vacuum the walk-off mats after the room, rolling them up and vacuuming underneath before you put them back.

instruction.heading: Hallways and door status
instruction.body: In a corridor, keep your back upright and hold the wand close to your body, sweeping it left and right as you walk ahead. Continue until the full width is covered, then disconnect and move on. Switch lights off once a room is complete. Door status is recorded with a colour dot placed on the middle hinge. A red dot means that the door stays locked before, during or after vacuuming. A green dot means that the door is shut without a lock afterwards. A yellow dot indicates the door is left as it was found. Follow the dot shown on each door, and do not change a door's state without the dot telling you to.

instruction.heading: Returning the machine
instruction.body: Replace the bag when it is about two-thirds full, so that suction is not lost. When the job is finished, return the machine and attachments to the cleaning cupboard. Check the bag and filters, then wipe the exterior of the machine, wind the cord neatly, and store the machine in its assigned place.

procedure: Put on gloves and eye protection, then inspect the bag or bin, filters, cord and plug.
Fit the backpack harness so the weight sits on the hips, and clip the tools to the waist belt.
Look for the site's marked vacuuming outlets and plug the cord in without unplugging any equipment.
Vacuum the room in a consistent counter-clockwise route, starting at the door and working around the perimeter.
Clean the corners, skirting boards and under-desk areas with the nozzle, moving chairs up to the desks as you go.
Lift any bin that has not been emptied, vacuum under it, and return it to its original spot.
Spot vacuum upholstered furniture with the upholstery tool where soil is visible.
Vacuum the entrance mats, rolling them up and vacuuming underneath, before putting them back.
Check the door status dot on each door and leave the door in the state the dot requires.
Replace the bag when it is about two-thirds full, then return the machine and attachments to the closet and store them.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner in an open office unplugs a computer to reach an outlet, and later drags the cord across the carpet so that the plug pulls out of the wall.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the cleaner have done instead?
workedExamples.reasoning: Use only the outlets marked for vacuuming, and never unplug equipment to make room. Leave slack in the cord and move it by its route, not by pulling. If equipment has been unplugged, reconnect it and tell the supervisor.

workedExamples.situation: A room has a door with a red dot on the hinge, and the cleaner is about to close it after vacuuming so the room looks tidy.
workedExamples.reasoning: A red dot means that the door must stay locked before, during or after vacuuming. Leave the door locked and do not change it. Check the dot on every door before you leave the room.

equipmentAndPpe: Back-pack vacuum or upright vacuum, with the bag or bin, filters and cord checked.
Upholstery nozzle, brush head and crevice tool.
Spare bags or filters for the machine.
Extension cord, where the site rules allow it.
Wet floor sign, used if the floor is wet or a hazard is present.

commonErrors.error: Unplugging a computer or other equipment to reach a vacuum outlet.
commonErrors.prevention: Use only the outlets set aside for vacuuming, and never unplug equipment to make room.

commonErrors.error: Pulling the cord to unplug the machine, which can break the plug.
commonErrors.prevention: Hold the plug and draw it out, keeping the cord slack during use.

commonErrors.error: Changing the state of a door without checking its dot.
commonErrors.prevention: Read the dot on the hinge before and after vacuuming, and leave the door as the dot requires.

commonErrors.error: Leaving a bin unemptied and vacuuming around it.
commonErrors.prevention: Lift the bin, vacuum under it, and return it to its spot.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Check the cord for cuts and bare wire before every use. Do not use a machine with a damaged cord or a missing earth pin. Tag it and report it.
Never vacuum water or liquid spills with a dry machine. Clean up the spill first, and use a wet floor sign if the floor is slippery.
Fit the backpack harness correctly and lift with the legs to reduce strain on the back.
Keep the cord out of walkways and off the stairs, and do not step over a cord that is taut across a path.

qualityStandard: Corners, edges and under-desk areas are vacuumed in every room.
Every bin is emptied or left in its original position with the floor beneath it vacuumed.
Walk-off mats are vacuumed on both sides and returned to position.
Each door is left in the state its dot requires.
No equipment has been unplugged to make room for the machine.
The machine is stored with a checked bag and filters and a wound cord.
documentationEvidence: Job record listing the rooms vacuumed, with the date and time.
Note of any door whose dot was unclear, or any outlet that was not marked, for supervisor review.
Note of any cord or plug defect found during the check, and the machine tagged out of use.
summary: Check the bag, filters, cord and plug before every job, and fit the harness correctly.
Vacuum in a fixed direction, corners and edges before the open floor, and empty or lift bins as you go.
Use only the marked outlets, and never unplug equipment to make room.
Read every door dot and leave each door as the dot requires.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which outlet should a vacuum be plugged into in an office that uses marked outlets for vacuuming?
options: Any outlet that is free, by unplugging the nearest computer
A marked vacuuming outlet, without unplugging any equipment
The outlet behind the desk with the cord taped across the floor

knowledgeChecks.question: A door has a red dot on its middle hinge. What should happen to the door?
options: It is closed but left unlocked afterwards
It is left as it was found, and the lock is reset afterwards
It stays locked before, during or after vacuuming

knowledgeChecks.question: When should the vacuum bag be replaced?
options: When it is about two-thirds full, so that suction is not lost
Only when the machine stops working completely
At the start of each room, before the walk-through is done
